author: Brian Christian; Tom Griffiths
title: Algorithms to Live By
reason: The introduction expressly promises practical suggestions for specific everyday problems. Eleven chapters are organized as methods to apply: optimal stopping, exploration, sorting, caching, scheduling, Bayes, overfitting, relaxation, randomness, networking and game theory. Under the repository's strict primary-purpose test, this is a mixed conceptual narrative whose main organizing purpose remains applying methods.
counterargument: Strong explanatory computer-science narrative and accessible history; no classroom exercises. This makes classification less clear than a textbook. Parent should resolve consistently with comparable previous exclusions. Do not infer exclusion merely from the word Algorithms.
evidence: Authorized introduction and stated practical aims
resolution: Superseded after independent gate review and fuller main-purpose reassessment. The explanatory account of computational constraints and human cognition is primary; practical applications do not establish instructional primacy. Eligible normalized record: data/tactical_algorithms_261018.json.
